title: ee.daemon.response.v1
description: Length-prefixed JSON response envelope returned by the optional `ee daemon` Unix-domain socket RPC introduced by bd-oja31 (SRR1 hot-mode skeleton). The wire framing matches `ee.daemon.request.v1`: 4-byte big-endian unsigned length followed by exactly that many bytes of UTF-8 JSON. `request_id` and `agent_id` echo the request envelope's ids so clients can multiplex if/when they reuse a connection and so daemon audit rows can attribute calls. `workspace_id` is echoed when the request carried it. The skeleton handles one request per accept; multiplexing is a follow-up. Exactly one of `result` or `error` is populated per response; the other MUST be absent. `degraded_codes[]` is structurally similar to the canonical `ee.response.v2` envelope's `degraded[]` array but reduced to bare code strings because the daemon RPC is local-first and intentionally does not duplicate the per-entry severity/repair fields the CLI envelope carries — the CLI client that consumes the daemon response maps the codes back onto the canonical envelope before returning to the user. `ee.daemon.capabilities` is the v1 discovery method clients use before attempting newer schemas or non-v1 methods; its result includes an `authorization` map that labels registered methods as `same_uid` or `same_uid_workspace`.

request_id.description: Echo of the request envelope's request_id. A response whose request_id does not match the most recent request on the same connection MUST be treated as a framing error and the connection torn down.

agent_id.description: Echo of the request envelope's agent_id. Pre-parse refusal responses use a sentinel such as `<unknown>` because the daemon could not safely read the caller's envelope.

workspace_id.description: Echo of the request envelope's optional workspace_id when present. Absent when the request omitted it or when the daemon refused before parsing the request envelope.

result.description: Method-specific success payload. For `ee.daemon.capabilities` this is an object with `protocol`, `request_schemas`, `response_schemas`, `methods`, `authorization`, and `forward_compat` fields. For `ee.daemon.echo` this is the request envelope's `params` value, returned in redaction-stable form when echo is explicitly enabled. For `ee.daemon.context` this field is absent in the current skeleton (the method returns `error.code = daemon_method_unauthorized` before authorization or `error.code = daemon_ann_warmload_not_yet_implemented` after authorization). The exact JSON value is method-specific; clients MUST NOT assume it is an object unless they are handling a method whose contract says so.

error.description: Populated when the method failed. The `code` vocabulary is method-specific; the seed codes used by the skeleton are `daemon_unknown_method`, `daemon_method_unauthorized`, `daemon_request_decode_failed`, `daemon_request_schema_mismatch`, and `daemon_ann_warmload_not_yet_implemented`. Additional codes may be added; consumers must tolerate unknown codes. The CLI client maps these onto the canonical `ee.error.v2` envelope before returning to the user.

degraded_codes.description: Bare degraded-code strings the daemon attached to the response. The CLI client maps each entry onto a full `ee.response.v2` `degraded[]` entry (severity/repair pulled from the canonical taxonomy in docs/degraded_code_taxonomy.md). Empty array when nothing degraded.
